FIND: The `section_terminator` regex (line ~109‑115) does not use `re.IGNORECASE`, so it will not terminate the ADMISSIBILITY block at lowercase section headers such as `novelty:`, `verified:`, etc. The `marker_match` regex for ADMISSIBILITY *does* use `re.IGNORECASE`; this inconsistency leaves the terminator blind to case variations that models can produce.
FOLLOW: When a model writes the next section header in lower‑ or mixed‑case, the regex fails to match. The block then consumes all remaining text until end‑of‑string or until a case‑matching header appears. This can engulf subsequent findings’ content. Downstream, the per‑gate `re.search` scans the oversized block; gate names from later findings may cause false‑PASS verdicts, or missing gates may still be reported as FAIL, garbling the feedback channel’s correction signal. Recovery requires manual intervention.
ANALYSE: HARD (data integrity). Premise: the parser must correctly isolate the ADMISSIBILITY block. Evidence: the `marker_match` uses `re.IGNORECASE`; the `section_terminator` does not. A test input with `novelty:` (lowercase) immediately after the block will not be recognized, causing runaway consumption. Verdict: CONFIRMED.
FIX: Add `re.IGNORECASE` to the `section_terminator` compilation.
